questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code applies the circuit breaker to carrier rate calls? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Northwind has been failing and its breaker is open. A quote request arrives for a lane, service level and weight band that was quoted successfully two hours ago. What does the caller get?
choices: One HTTP attempt that times out after 3 seconds, then the cached quote.
Two retries with backoff against Northwind, then a 503 because the breaker is open.
The cached quote with IsEstimate set to true, returned without any network call being made.
A 503 immediately, because a broken circuit is not one of the exceptions the service catches.

questions.prompt: Northwind starts answering 422 for a malformed ZIP on a large share of requests for an hour. What is the effect on the breaker?
choices: None: 4xx responses are not in the handled set, and the client converts them to InvalidQuoteRequestException, so the breaker records them as successes.
It opens once at least 10 calls have been sampled in 30 seconds and half of them were 422.
It stays closed but the retry policy retries each 422 twice.
It opens only if the 422 responses also exceed the 3 second timeout.

questions.prompt: The AddPolicyHandler callback runs for every outgoing request. What makes the breaker able to trip at all?
choices: CarrierRateClient is registered as a typed client, which makes the HttpClient a singleton.
IMemoryCache stores the failure counts between requests.
The retry policy is outermost, so it carries the failure count from one attempt to the next across requests.
The callback returns the instance cached per carrier by CarrierPolicyRegistry, so every request reports its outcome to the same breaker state.
